occurrences.lead_in: Look for other clean water in the house
occurrences.review_topic: tap-water heater versus household heating system and ice contamination
occurrences.editorial_observation: CDC lists tap-water heater tanks and uncontaminated ice as conditional possible sources; original draft says 'water heater tank, melted ice cubes and similar sources' without both specific caveats.
occurrences.suggested_human_action: Evaluate whether to clarify potable water-heater distinction and uncontaminated-ice condition in the reader-facing sentence; ensure local-authority warnings remain.

occurrences.lead_in: Stop and ask what might be upstream.
occurrences.review_topic: microbial sewage/waste versus fuel or toxic chemical contamination
occurrences.editorial_observation: CDC warns outdoor water can have animal/human waste and requires treatment for germs, but says water suspected to contain fuel/toxic chemicals cannot be made safe. The manuscript lumps 'fuel, chemicals or waste' together as an always-use-another-source decision; cautious advice may be reasonable but this precise citation does not make the categories equivalent.
occurrences.suggested_human_action: Check whether revised wording should explicitly distinguish microbiological contamination from chemical/fuel contamination, retaining conservative guidance where source or local advisory is uncertain.

occurrences.lead_in: Ready.gov asks you to consider languages spoken in the household
occurrences.review_topic: Ready.gov language planning claim independently inaccessible on this run
occurrences.editorial_observation: The frozen source fragment states that Ready.gov includes household languages as a consideration, but a fresh direct page fetch returned HTTP 403; this run cannot independently corroborate the current page wording or date.
occurrences.suggested_human_action: Have an independent reviewer inspect the current Ready.gov page or official cached/accessibly rendered substitute and record exact page/date/claim line; do not silently mark verified.
